abyssinian.fun_fact: Often depicted in ancient Egyptian art — one of the oldest known breeds.

american_bobtail.fun_fact: They love to play fetch — very dog-like personality!

american_curl.fun_fact: Born with straight ears that curl backward within days of birth.

american_shorthair.fun_fact: One of the most popular cat breeds in the USA, descended from working cats.

american_wirehair.fun_fact: Their unique wiry coat is a natural mutation first seen in 1966.

balinese.fun_fact: Sometimes called the 'long-haired Siamese' — same vocal personality!

bengal.fun_fact: Descended from Asian Leopard Cats — wild look, domestic heart.

birman.fun_fact: Legend says Birmans were sacred temple cats blessed by a golden goddess.

bombay.fun_fact: Bred to look like a miniature black panther — nicknamed 'parlor panther'.

british_shorthair.fun_fact: The Cheshire Cat from Alice in Wonderland was inspired by this breed!

burmese.fun_fact: All Burmese worldwide trace back to a single female cat brought to the USA in 1930.

chartreux.fun_fact: French monks at the Grande Chartreuse monastery are said to have bred this cat.

chausie.fun_fact: Descended from the Jungle Cat (Felis chaus) — one of the closest to wild cats.

cornish_rex.fun_fact: Has only the soft undercoat — no guard hairs, giving a uniquely curly look.

cymric.fun_fact: Essentially a long-haired Manx — they share the taillessness gene.

cyprus.fun_fact: One of the oldest domesticated cat breeds — evidence dates back 9,500 years!

devon_rex.fun_fact: Called 'pixie cats' due to their large ears and elfin face.

donskoy.fun_fact: Hairlessness is caused by a dominant gene — unlike Sphynx which is recessive.

egyptian_mau.fun_fact: The only naturally spotted domestic cat breed — spots are in the coat, not just the skin!

european_shorthair.fun_fact: The most common cat in Europe, descended from cats the Romans spread across the continent.

exotic_shorthair.fun_fact: Nicknamed 'the lazy man's Persian' — same look, easier-to-maintain coat.

german_rex.fun_fact: One of the first curly-coated breeds, discovered in Germany after World War II.

havana_brown.fun_fact: The only all-brown cat breed — their rich mahogany color inspired the name 'Havana'.

himalayan.fun_fact: A Persian × Siamese cross — Persian body with Siamese color points.

japanese_bobtail.fun_fact: The 'Maneki-neko' lucky waving cat figurine is modeled after this breed!

karelian_bobtail.fun_fact: A rare natural breed from Karelian forests with a pom-pom tail.

khao_manee.fun_fact: An ancient Thai royal cat — once exclusive to royalty.

korat.fun_fact: In Thailand, Korats are considered good luck and gifted to newlyweds.

korean_bobtail.fun_fact: A natural breed from Korea with a distinctive short, pom-pom tail.

kurilian_bobtail.fun_fact: Natural hunters from the remote Kuril Islands — excellent fishers!

laperm.fun_fact: Born bald, they grow a unique curly coat — each cat's curls are different!

lykoi.fun_fact: Called the 'Werewolf Cat' — their patchy coat gives a spooky, Halloween appearance.

maine_coon.fun_fact: The largest domestic cat breed — males can reach 18 lbs! They love water.

manx.fun_fact: Naturally tailless due to a genetic mutation — can be fully tailless or have a stub.

mekong_bobtail.fun_fact: Named after the Mekong River — historically kept by royalty across Southeast Asia.

munchkin.fun_fact: Their short legs are a natural mutation — they can still run surprisingly fast!

nebelung.fun_fact: Named after German mythology ('creature of the mist') — their shimmery coat inspired it.

norwegian_forest_cat.fun_fact: Vikings likely kept these cats on ships to catch mice during long voyages!

ocicat.fun_fact: Looks wild but is entirely domestic — created by accident from Siamese × Abyssinian crosses.

oregon_rex.fun_fact: An extremely rare curly-coated breed — now considered an extinct separate variety.

oriental_shorthair.fun_fact: Comes in over 300 color and pattern combinations — more than any other breed!

persian.fun_fact: Their luxurious coat can grow up to 6 inches long and needs daily brushing.

peterbald.fun_fact: Created in 1994 by crossing a Donskoy with an Oriental Shorthair.

pixie_bob.fun_fact: Rumored to descend from bobcats — DNA tests show they are fully domestic.

ragamuffin.fun_fact: They go completely limp when held — nicknamed 'puppy cats'.

ragdoll.fun_fact: Named 'Ragdoll' because they go limp and floppy when you pick them up!

russian_blue.fun_fact: Their double coat has silver-tipped guard hairs giving a shimmering blue glow.

safari.fun_fact: A rare hybrid from domestic cats × wild Geoffroy's Cat from South America.

savannah.fun_fact: The tallest domestic cat — crossed with Serval, they can jump over 8 feet high!

scottish_fold.fun_fact: All Scottish Folds trace back to one barn cat named Susie, found in Scotland in 1961.

selkirk_rex.fun_fact: Named after the Selkirk Mountains — the only curly-coated breed named after a person!

serengeti.fun_fact: Bred to look like a Serval — from Bengal × Oriental Shorthair crosses, no wild blood.

siberian.fun_fact: Russia's national cat — centuries-old forest breed, and semi-hypoallergenic!

singapura.fun_fact: The smallest domestic cat breed — adults weigh only 4–8 pounds!

sokoke.fun_fact: One of the rarest breeds — discovered living wild in Kenya's Arabuko-Sokoke Forest.

somali.fun_fact: Called the 'fox cat' — essentially a long-haired Abyssinian with a fluffy tail.

sphynx.fun_fact: Despite looking hairless, they're covered in fine peach-fuzz and feel like warm suede!

thai.fun_fact: The traditional round-faced Siamese, preserved by Thai cat fanciers.

tonkinese.fun_fact: A Siamese × Burmese cross — they inherited the best traits of both!

toyger.fun_fact: Bred to look like a miniature tiger — 'Toyger' = 'Toy Tiger'. Still being developed!

turkish_angora.fun_fact: The Ankara Zoo has a special program to preserve this ancient Turkish breed.

turkish_van.fun_fact: Known as 'the swimming cat' — they genuinely love water and are strong swimmers!

ukrainian_levkoy.fun_fact: Created in Ukraine in 2004 — a Donskoy × Scottish Fold cross with folded ears and no fur.

ural_rex.fun_fact: A natural curly breed from the Ural Mountains, independently evolved from other Rex breeds.

vankedisi.fun_fact: The all-white version of the Turkish Van — 'Vankedisi' means 'Van cat' in Turkish.
